name: The Saltbitten Mate
persona: A blunt, weathered sailor keeping the book. Short sentences, no poetry, dry humour. Speaks plainly of hard work and hard weather. Ship: 'we'. Island: a gruff steward, 'we'.

ship.founder: This book is mine now. {name}{rankc}. She's a {home} {type} and she answers to me. I'll keep it plain.
ship.successor: New hand on the log. {name}{rankc}. I'll set down what happens and not dress it up.
ship.mutiny: The old man's gone over the side and the lads handed me the book. {name}. I don't know the half of it yet, but I'll learn her.
ship.rogue: No more honest work. Flag's black and the book's mine. {name}{rankc}. Say what you like about it.
ship.prize: She struck to us and I took her. {name}{rankc}. Her log's mine to fill now.
ship.recovered: A hunter caught us cold and that was that. {name}{rankc}. My job's to bring her home clean and keep the book.

island.founder: I've got the running of {place} now, and the ledger with it. {name}{rankc}. Plain words, plain accounts.
island.overthrow: They dragged the last one out by the collar and gave me the seal. {name}{rankc}. {place}'s mine to run.
island.successor: {place} passes to me. {name}{rankc}. I keep the book from here.

ship.pirate: We're still out here, flag up{bounty}. Come and take us.
ship.default: Still afloat, still working her, out of {home}.

island.haven: The black flag flies over us now. No law, no ledger worth keeping.
island.default: {population} souls, and the port holds. That's the account.

quiet.ship: Not much to write. Fair winds, full holds, quiet water. I'll take it.
quiet.island: Quiet books this year. Trade in, trade out, nobody bleeding. Good.

say: {we} ran {foe} down, took {goods} bales and {gold}g off her, and let her go — she wasn't worth the powder to finish
{we} boarded {foe}, cleaned out {goods} crates and {gold}g, and cut her loose to limp home and tell the tale
{foe} struck quick — {goods} casks and {gold}g into {our} hold, and no blood spilled worth mentioning
{we} took what {foe} was carrying — {goods} chests and {gold}g — and left her the rest, which was mostly water
{we} came up on {foe} and helped {us} to {goods} bales and {gold}g, then waved her off
{foe} gave up {goods} crates and {gold}g without much fuss — sensible of her
{we} stripped {foe} of {goods} casks and {gold}g and sent her on, lighter and wiser
{we} put enough holes in {foe} that she gave up and went down — cargo and all, nothing saved
{we} sank {foe} clean — whatever she carried is fish food now
{foe} wouldn't strike, so {we} kept firing till the sea took her — her own fault
{we} hammered {foe} at the waterline and watched her slide under, hold full, no prize for {us}
{we} traded shot with {foe} till she filled and sank — the goods went down with her, worse luck
{foe} went under {our} guns before she could yield, and took every crate with her
{we} broke {foe} up and sent her down — no boarding, no loot, just a dead ship and a quiet sea
{foe} came at {us} looking for an easy day — {we} gave her powder instead, and down she went
{we} weren't the soft mark {foe} took {us} for — {we} shot her under and carried on
{foe} tried to board {us} and {we} sank her for it — should've picked a slower ship
{we} stood off {foe} with everything {we} had, and it was her that ended up on the bottom
{foe} thought {us} cargo — turned out {we} bite, and she learned it too late
{we} put {foe} down when she came for {us}, and lost nothing but a morning and some shot
{foe} closed to take {us}, and {we} closed to bury her — she went first
{we} ran {foe} down at last and sank her — one less wolf on the lanes, and good riddance
{we} chased {foe} halfway to nowhere and put her under — took long enough
{foe} had it coming a long while — {we} caught her and gave it to her
{we} cornered {foe} and finished the job — no prize wanted, just her gone
{foe} won't be robbing anyone else — {we} saw to that, personal
{we} tracked {foe} down and sank her flag and all, and slept fine after
{we} put {foe} on the bottom where she belonged — the lanes are the cleaner for it
